title: [bug] npm package missing scripts/lib/compile.mjs — postinstall fails on every install
Broken site/pointer workflow: router consolidation left no working URL or installed skill for rule-of-5-universal
description:
2026-09 router consolidation (incitaciones-oyz) broke the deployed-site URL workflow in two ways:

1. rule-of-5-universal has no usable URL: manifest distilled -> content/distilled/pointers/rule-of-5-universal.md, a 'moved' stub. Actual content lives at content/distilled/review/references/rule-of-5-universal/SKILL.md, never linked by site. llms.txt/index.html title links target 'source' (router-architecture essay).
2. site/build.sh collects references with single-level glob: review-unified.md and llms-full.txt silently omit all nested router members (rule-of-5-universal, code-review, parallel-review with their references/).

Installed-skill workflow also broken: pointer SKILL.md instructs reading references/rule-of-5-universal/SKILL.md relative to install dir where nothing exists (live-triggered and confirmed).

Design decision (Rule-of-5 review, converged): 'compiled pointers' doctrine. Pointer = build artifact: full member content + provenance banner, compiled from router member dir into every output channel (site, npm/pi package, install.sh). disable_model_invocation already makes full-content pointers zero-cost always-on, so pointer deletion (incitaciones-mtw) is unnecessary -- pointers become permanent.

Fix plan:
- manifest: add pointer_for field to all 8 pointer entries
- build.sh: recursive reference collection; generate {member}-unified.md per router member; compile pointer pages as banner+content; fix title links to content not source; same recursion fix for llms-full.txt
- generate-pi-resources.mjs / install: pointers ship full compiled content
- AGENTS.md: pointer policy amended -- regenerate, never delete (supersedes incitaciones-mtw)
- validation: sync-manifest asserts pointer_for targets exist
- regenerate skills catalog
close_reason: Compiled-pointers doctrine shipped: pointer_for on 8 pointers, shared compiler (scripts/lib/compile.mjs), site member URLs + compiled pointer pages, recursive unified docs/llms-full, self-contained installed pointers (flat installs re-synced live), pointer gate in sync-manifest, AGENTS.md policy amendment. review skill-eval 2/2; all gates green.

title: Consolidate overlapping skill families (router + references/)
description: Always-on skill cost is ~5,900 tokens/conversation (measured: rendered <available_skills> block = 23,246 chars, 70 skills). Consolidation is the dominant fix: ~2,200 net token savings. Merge into routers with references/: session x6->1 (close, park, next, renew, resume-handoff, create-handoff), review x7->1 (code-review, rule-of-5, rule-of-5-universal, parallel-review, multi-agent-review, guided-review, red-team-review), planning x6->2, *-diagnostician x12->1 (shared skeleton, distinct content — router desc must enumerate domains), docs x4->2, prompt-meta x3->1. Note: diagnostician bodies are NOT identical (different personas/GUARDs/taxonomies/step counts) — split content into references/, keep router SKILL.md thin. Blast radius: manifest.json entries+bundles, scripts/generate-pi-resources.mjs, install.sh, CHANGELOG, /skill:name names, version-pinned installed copies in other repos (npm:0.9.0). Ship old names as thin pointer skills for one release, then remove.
close_reason: Closed

title: renew skill: delegate whisper context load to turu CLI (drop legacy path pipeline)
description: Session skill references/renew/SKILL.md step 7 hand-rolls repo_url/branch_slug derivation (git remote get-url | sed) and reads legacy files (context.md/plan.md) from ~/.whisper/repos/<raw-url>/branches/<slug>. title: grill-me skill: actor bundles multiple questions per turn despite explicit one-question protocol
description:
Second catch by the skill-eval harness (incitaciones-env slice 2): run-to-run, the actor nondeterministically violates the skill's protocol step 4 ('Ask questions one at a time') — run2 asked 3-4 sub-questions in one turn (cacheability + staleness tolerance + read-your-writes + write ratio). Judge: multiple_questions_bundled_in_one_turn=true, single_focused_question_asked=false. Run1 failed on a different signal (context_inspectable_question_was_asked) — variance, not a rubric bug. Evidence: .cache/skill-eval/grill-me/ (gitignored; regenerate: just skill-eval grill-me).

MUST: grill-me distilled (content/distilled/grill-me.md) makes the one-question-per-turn contract the headline output rule (e.g., 'Output exactly ONE question per turn — bundling questions violates this skill').
MUST: just skill-eval grill-me exits 0 (2/2 runs PASS) after the fix.
METER: just skill-eval grill-me.
ANTI-GOAL: do not weaken the rubric (single_focused_question stays) or make the fixture easier.
acceptance_criteria: just skill-eval grill-me green 2/2 across 3 consecutive invocations; no rubric weakening
close_reason: Fixed: grill-me 1.0.1 (source content/prompt-task-grill-me.md + distilled content/distilled/grill-me.md, lockstep). 'One question per turn' is now a hard rule with a queued-decisions escape hatch; inspection-intent convention added to step 5 (also fixes the run1 failure mode seen pre-fix). Meter: just skill-eval grill-me — PASS 3/3 consecutive invocations (AC: 3 consecutive), 6/6 actor runs, no rubric/fixture weakening.

title: issues skill: actor slices plans into horizontal layer tickets despite create-issues guidance
description:
First genuine catch by the skill-eval harness (incitaciones-env slice 2, 2026-09-15): given a CSV-export plan (backend route + frontend button + docs + tests), the actor produced SIX horizontal layer tickets (serializer / route / button / tests-by-layer / docs) — the exact anti-pattern create-issues encodes. Judge verdict: horizontal_layer_tickets=true, quantified_must_gates=false, runnable_meter=false, 2/2 runs FAIL. Evidence artifacts: .cache/skill-eval/issues/run{1,2}-actor.md (gitignored — excerpt in this body; regenerate with: just skill-eval issues).

MUST: create-issues reference content makes the vertical-slice rule operationally explicit at the decision point (e.g., 'one issue per user-visible outcome; if the title names a layer (backend/frontend/docs/tests-only), merge it into the outcome slice').
MUST: just skill-eval issues exits 0 (2/2 runs PASS) after the fix.
METER: just skill-eval issues.
ANTI-GOAL: do not weaken the eval rubric or fixture to make the current behavior pass.
acceptance_criteria: just skill-eval issues green 2/2; no rubric/fixture weakening
close_reason:
Fixed in 186b83a (create-issues 1.4.1) + 0f6f229 (harness flatten fix), skills catalog d52e1d8.
Root cause was twofold: (1) skill said "prefer vertical slices" — preference language didn't hold; now a hard TITLE LINT runs on every drafted title before presenting (layer-named titles merge into their outcome slice), source + distilled in lockstep v1.4.1; (2) the skill-eval harness's maxdepth-1 flatten silently dropped multi-file router members, so the actor never saw the create-issues content at all — flatten now recursive.
Meter: just skill-eval issues → PASS 2/2, 6/6 success signals, 0 failure signals. No rubric/fixture weakening (anti-goal held).
Attribution caveat: lint edit and content-delivery fix landed together; isolated contribution not measured.

title: Decide install-layer policy: router member skills ship standalone next to their router
description:
Audit finding (CORR-003, sharpened by Rule-of-5 2026-09-16): mutual-distinctness of descriptions is violated at the INSTALL layer, not just in manifest text. Router members (code-review, red-team-review, parallel-review, plan-review, multi-agent-review) are emitted as standalone skill dirs by generate-skills-dir and installed alongside the review router (present in both repo .agents/skills/ and global ~/.agents/skills/). At runtime, 'red-team review this code' has two competing entry points: the standalone global skill AND /skill:review red-team mode. The router's description even claims 'specs, or docs' territory while specification-review/research-review/design-review remain live siblings.

MUST: decision doc — either (a) install-time suppression of member standalones when the router is installed, or (b) explicit dual-path design with disambiguation clauses in both descriptions, or (c) document intentional overlap.
MUST: if (a), keep /skill:<member> invocations working (compat-pointer precedent, cf. beads mtw).
ANTI-GOAL: no manifest hand-editing of skills/ catalog (generated artifact).
acceptance_criteria: Policy documented in content/ (router architecture doc) + emission change shipped or overlap explicitly documented; no runtime ambiguity for 'red-team' and 'spec review' phrasings
notes: Meter note: rbn's sync-manifest overlap check (its MUST 3) is the runnable Meter for this ticket's AC 'no runtime ambiguity for spec review phrasings' — verify against that check rather than ad-hoc greps. Soft ordering: rbn before final 1r7 verification; the policy DECISION itself is not blocked.

title: Add just security-audit gate for distilled skills (supply-chain framing)
description:
Audit finding (B166/Nubank: skills are supply chain, not config — they steer code agents generate on other machines; npm-published incitaciones ships to third parties). Current checks are manual greps (token patterns, curl|bash, dangerous rm) — audit on 2026-09-16 was clean, but nothing enforces it.

MUST: just security-audit scans content/distilled/ + content/prompt-*.md for risk patterns: hardcoded credentials, curl|bash, rm -rf on variables/globs, permission-escalation instructions, disable-safety instructions.
MUST: wire into sync-manifest (or pre-push) so publication is gated.
ANTI-GOAL: no false-positive-heavy linting; patterns must be reviewable and each hit actionable.
acceptance_criteria: just security-audit green on current corpus; runs as part of sync-manifest; documented in CONTRIBUTING.md
notes: PRE-002 co-modification note: justfile (sync-manifest recipe) shared with env+rbn — both extend sync-manifest; land security-audit hook in its own commit, rebase after rbn.
close_reason: Shipped in 827575c: scripts/security-audit.sh (245-file corpus scan, 6 pattern classes, corpus-evidenced advisory filter), wired into just sync-manifest before version bump, negative-tested (3 injected risk classes detected), documented in CONTRIBUTING.md. All AC met; anti-goal respected (zero false positives on current corpus).

title: Add trigger clauses to 32 bare skill descriptions; budget-capped
description:
Audit finding (B171: description is the routing contract, written as 'use only when...'): 32 of 38 live prompt descriptions are content summaries with no trigger clause (full name list captured in audit session 2026-09-16; regenerable via python3 manifest scan for descriptions without /trigger|use when|use only when|use for/i).

MUST: capture ALWAYS-ON token baseline BEFORE any edit (compare against the oyz consolidation win of ~47% — do not erode it).
MUST: each addition <= 10 words, written as routing contract ('Use when X') not feature copy.
MUST: validate mutual distinctness — extend just sync-manifest with an overlap check (flag descriptions sharing trigger domains without a distinguishing clause).
ANTI-GOAL: no bulk rewrites without the before/after token measurement.
acceptance_criteria: sync-manifest overlap check green; token delta measured and within agreed budget; 32 descriptions carry trigger clauses
notes:
PRE-002 co-modification note: content/manifest.json shared with env+1r7; justfile (sync-manifest recipe) shared with env+8am. Sequence manifest edits env→rbn→1r7.
Cohort persisted (was hidden conversational context, EXEC/CLRT remediation 2026-09-16). The 32 bare descriptions: agent-value-alignment, specification-review, commit, debug, describe-pr, research-codebase, design-practice, pre-mortem, tdd, narrative-article, optionality-review, design-review, research-review, ui-align, bias-audit, abstraction-miner, context-guardian, resonant-refactor, test-friction, test-abstraction-miner, pwa-accessibility-review, file-headers, edge-case-discovery, adversarial-stakeholder-evaluation, formal-verification-evaluator, doc-link-verifier, systematic-housekeeping, grill-me, anti-slop-prose, project-status-report, codebase-cartography, diagnostician. Regenerate: manifest scan, description without /trigger|use when|use only when|use for/i.
Meter (named): baseline = sum of manifest description word counts + one real pi session system-prompt capture, both recorded in .cache/ before any edit; after-state must not exceed baseline + 10 words x 32 (proxy token cost = words x 1.3).
close_reason:
Shipped in 48ec986. All three MUSTs met:
(1) Baseline captured BEFORE edits: 577 description words / ~750 proxy tokens across 38 live prompts (.cache/rbn-baseline.json).
(2) 32 trigger clauses added, each <=10 words (delta +242 words, within the 320-word budget); review-family exclusives carry "use only when".
(3) sync-manifest now gates on trigger-clause coverage + pairwise distinctness (scripts/trigger-overlap.py, negative-tested — injected multi-clause overlap caught).
AC: overlap check green, delta measured and within budget, 38/38 live descriptions carry clauses. Installed skills refresh at next release (8pv). ajp gets live-session evidence to validate routing improvements.

title: Build active skill-eval harness: rerun manifest eval rubrics on model change
description:
Audit finding (Rule-of-5 reviewed 2026-09-16, CORR-001 corrected): manifest eval rubrics (14/47 prompts have task_types/success_signals/failure_signals/stages/references) are consumed only PASSIVELY by scripts/analyze-traces.js:698,739,772 (trace labeling via trace-insights). Nothing actively executes a skill and checks its rubric — the B171 corpus gap: 'skills without evals are wishful thinking; rerun evals on every model change.' A model upgrade could silently break skills (FactSet attention-decay failure mode) with no detection.

MUST: just skill-eval [NAME] executes a skill against its manifest rubric via an LLM judge (pi), scoring success/failure signals; pass requires signal-majority agreement across 2 runs (LLM judges are stochastic).
MUST: essentials-first priority ordering to bound cost (38 skills x reruns is real money).
MUST: add eval rubrics to the 4/8 essentials missing them (review, issues, session, grill-me) — re-verify cohort at implementation time via the manifest eval-field scan (see NOTES).
MUST: wire 'rerun skill-eval on model change' into the release checklist (CHANGELOG/release process).
ANTI-GOAL: no passive-only labeling extensions; the harness must EXECUTE the skill, not grade old traces.
acceptance_criteria: just skill-eval runs for any eval-bearing skill and exits nonzero on rubric failure; release checklist references it; review, issues, session AND grill-me have rubrics
notes:
CORRECTION of description aside: eval-bearing cohort is exactly the 14 listed in manifest; essentials lacking rubrics = 4/8 (review, issues, session, grill-me), not 3/8. Verify cohort at implementation time via: python3 -c list of prompts with .get('eval').
PRE-002 co-modification note: content/manifest.json shared with 1r7+rbn; justfile shared with rbn+8am. Land manifest description edits in separate commits; rebase in rbn→8am order.
Tracer-bullet increment (SCOPE remediation): slice 1 = 'just skill-eval commit' green end-to-end on an existing rubric-bearing skill; slices 2-4 = rubrics for review/issues/session/grill-me, essentials-first ordering, release-checklist wiring. Regression suite to keep green: just validate && just sync-manifest && just trace-insights (analyze-traces.js:698,739,772 consumers unaffected).
SLICE 1 SHIPPED (see git log): just skill-eval commit green end-to-end — actor/judge separation, 2-run agreement, FAIL path verified (judge flags git-add-dot + generic message; prose output rejected). Release-checklist wiring done (README + CONTRIBUTING). REMAINING on this ticket: eval rubrics for review, issues, session, grill-me (the 4/8 essentials lacking them) — each needs rubric + fixture, then just skill-eval <name> green.
close_reason: All AC met and shipped (8ea9c12 slice 1, 5e5eb95 slice 2): harness runs any eval-bearing skill, rerun ritual wired into release docs, essentials 7/7 rubrics+fixtures. issues/grill-me eval red by design — fixes tracked in e5v and tth.

description: Follow-up to incitaciones-oyz (Rule-of-5 EDGE-001). 36 former trigger surfaces collapsed into 7 router descriptions + mode tables. title: Trim over-long skill descriptions selectively (>150 chars)
description: Descriptions total 7,931 chars (~1,982 tok) across 70 skills and are the largest trimmable always-on component. Measured ceiling: capping ALL descs at 100 chars saves only 584 tok (7,931 -> 5,593 chars) — most descs are already short. CONSTRAINT: description is the model's only trigger signal. Blind <=100-char capping risks wrong-skill activation for near-duplicate pairs (anti-slop 230ch vs anti-slop-prose 159ch rely on descriptive detail to disambiguate). Do: trim only descriptions >150 chars; preserve distinguishing phrases; keep disambiguation pairs deliberately differentiated. Expected saving: ~400-580 tok.
close_reason: Closed

title: pi install update does not re-sync skills on version bump
description:
When pi install or pi update --force installs a new version of an npm package (e.g., incitaciones from 0.3.0 to 0.3.1), it refreshes the npm package in .pi/agent/npm/node_modules/ but does NOT re-copy the skills from pi-package/skills/ to the skills directories. This leaves stale installed skills at the old version.

The skills only get copied on the first pi install. Subsequent pi update reports success but leaves the skills directory untouched.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Install incitaciones@0.3.0: pi install npm:incitaciones
2. Bump to 0.3.1, publish, regenerate pi-package
3. Remove stale skills from ~/.agents/skills/
4. Run: pi update npm:incitaciones --force
5. Observe: skills directory is NOT repopulated, npm package is updated

Expected: pi update should re-copy skills from the packages pi-package/skills/ to the skills directory on version change.

Two active skill directories were observed: ~/.agents/skills and ~/.config/agents/skills with different inodes but identical content
acceptance_criteria:
1. Pi update --force re-copies skills from pi-package/skills/ to the configured skills directories
2. Installed-version stamp in SKILL.md frontmatter reflects the new version
3. Removing the skills directory and running pi update restores it
4. Regression: skills from unrelated packages are not altered
close_reason: Fixed in 0.3.2. generate-pi-resources.mjs now includes reSyncFlatInstallSkills() that detects and re-syncs flat-install skill dirs on postinstall. Tested: removing skills from ~/.agents/skills/ + running the generator restores them with npm:0.3.2 stamp.

title: Add 'just release' recipe automating the version/catalog chicken-and-egg
description: npm version patch bumps package.json, and generate-skills-dir embeds installed-version from it, so validate-skills-dir (pre-push) always fails on a release push. Proven manual sequence (v0.10.1): finalize CHANGELOG → npm version patch → node scripts/generate-skills-dir.mjs + commit → git tag -f v<N> → git push --follow-tags.
